territorial_scope.description: Designations are addressed to named undertakings and their listed core platform services, made by the European Commission under the DMA.

evidence.quote: the European Commission designated for the first time six gatekeepers - Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta, Microsoft - under the Digital Markets Act (DMA)

summary.short: Commission decisions designating named undertakings as gatekeepers, and their core platform services, under the Digital Markets Act. First designations 6 September 2023; later additions include Apple iPadOS (29 April 2024), Booking (13 May 2024), and one undesignation (Meta, Facebook Marketplace, 23 April 2025).
summary.long: The document is a Commission portal page summarising designation decisions under the Digital Markets Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/1925). On 6 September 2023 the Commission designated six gatekeepers: Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta and Microsoft. On 29 April 2024 Apple was designated for its iPadOS, and on 13 May 2024 Booking was designated for its online intermediation service Booking.com. On 23 April 2025 Meta was undesignated for its online intermediation service Facebook Marketplace. The page states that 23 core platform services are currently designated and lists them by provider with case numbers, including Google Search, Android Mobile, AppStore, iOS, Safari, TikTok, Facebook, WhatsApp and Windows PC OS. It refers to resources on submissions, the designation process and information on acquisitions under Article 14. The portal text does not itself set out designation criteria or operative obligations; these appear in the designation decisions linked from the page.

relations.note: The text names only the Digital Markets Act (DMA). The regulation number and Article 3 appear only in registry metadata, not in the text.

notes: Source is a Commission web portal summary, not the designation decisions themselves (linked as Download the Designation Decision, not fetched), so text_version is partial. Registry metadata cites Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 and Article 3; the text does not. The intro says 23 core platform services are designated; the lists total 23. Meta was undesignated for Facebook Marketplace on 23 April 2025, which is not in its list. Case numbers shared across services as written: DMA.100011 (Google Maps, Google Shopping), DMA.100020 (Facebook, Instagram), DMA.100024 (WhatsApp, Messenger). The designating Commission is not coded as an entity because its powers are not stated in this text. No LEI or ticker verified.

thresholds.note: The document is a list of Commission gatekeeper designations and core platform services. It states no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. The Article 3 designation thresholds are not reproduced here and are not coded. The count of 23 core platform services is descriptive, not a threshold.

definitions.note: The document uses terms such as 'gatekeeper', 'core platform service' and 'online intermediation service' but does not define them. It refers to Article 14 and Article 3 without quoting definitions.

obligations.note: This document is a web page listing Commission designations of gatekeepers and core platform services under the Digital Markets Act. It states no operative duties on any addressee. It refers to Article 14 only for submitting information on acquisitions and to resources for gatekeepers, without stating obligations. Any duties would sit in the underlying designation decisions and the regulation they cite, which are not part of the fetched text.

enforcement.note: This document is a portal listing of Commission gatekeeper designations and core platform services. It contains no sanction, fine, penalty or enforcement provisions, and the designation record does not set any.
